html:
Nicholas I was the ruler of Montenegro from 1860 to 1918, first as prince and from 1910 as king. He was born in 1841 at Njeguši.

He led Montenegro through the wars of 1876 to 1878 that won recognition and new land. He built schools, roads and the first constitution, of 1905, but ruled in an old style. Several of his daughters married into royal houses, one becoming queen of Italy, and he was called the father in law of Europe. In World War I Austria occupied the country and he went into exile. In 1918 the Podgorica Assembly deposed him and joined Montenegro to Serbia. He died in exile in France.
